Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Housing Authority on any matter listed on the agenda or
on any other matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the
Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address the Housing Authority, please complete the card that is provided at
the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. The Housing Authority will hear
public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Housing
Authority will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or
unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The Housing Authority may direct staff to investigate
and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Housing Authority meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Housing Authority:
  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the Housing Authority as a whole and not directed to individual
  Commissioners.
Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted
listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the
agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons
with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the
City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Housing Authority regarding any item on this
agenda after it has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk
Boulevard during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.,
every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at
recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

   ATTACHMENT 1
  Housing Authority
  Check Summary Information Sheet

The warrants in the Housing Authority agenda report are for housing assistance payments
made under the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. The payee has a choice of
receiving the housing assistance payment via direct deposit, which is an electronic fund
transfer made directly to the payee’s bank account, or by paper check.

In the check summary report, the direct deposits are listed first as direct deposits, and then
the checks follow. Each direct deposit and paper check represents payment for 1 to 20
tenants depending upon the number of Section 8 tenants the payee has.

The payee is the property owner or designated management company. The property owner
or manager may be a corporation, partnership, trust, or individual. The payee name is the
owner or manager’s legal business or individual name, which must match Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) records. Here are some common abbreviations used in business names:

LLC = Limited Liability Company

LP = Limited Partnership

DBA = “Doing Business As”

LTD = Limited

Checks made out to the City of Norwalk Housing Authority represent the Family Self
Sufficiency (FSS) escrow deposits. These checks are deposited into the Housing Authority’s
bank account where the funds earn interest and are kept in escrow until the FSS participant
successfully completes the program at which time they receive the balance of their account.

Norwalk Housing Investors, LP is the owner of Center Pointe Villas at 14100 San Antonio
and 11856 Orange. Payments are for Section 8 participants living in these buildings.

Payments to housing authorities, such as the Orange County Housing Authority and San
Bernardino County Housing, represent reimbursements for our participants who have
transferred to those jurisdictions under portability.

Please call Bethani Cardenas at ext. 5588 if you have any questions.

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. NHA-178 - APPROVING THE NORWALK HOUSING
  AUTHORITY SECTION 8 MANAGEMENT ASSESSMENT PROGRAM
  CERTIFICATION FOR FISCAL YEAR ENDING JUNE 30, 2026

Background:

The Section 8 Management Assessment Program (SEMAP) is designed to assist the United
States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) with assessing housing authority
performance on 14 key indicators. In order to rate the performance of housing authorities, HUD
uses annual audit reports, family data reported by the housing authority, budget utilization
reports, and on-site reviews.

Each year, the Norwalk Housing Authority (NHA) is required to perform a self-evaluation and
submit a SEMAP Certification to HUD within 60 days of the fiscal year end. In completing the
certification, case files were randomly selected and evaluated by the Housing Manager in
accordance with SEMAP criteria and HUD sampling requirements.

The NHA met all SEMAP standards and anticipates a high-performance rating, consistent with
previous years' high ratings. The results of the SEMAP review demonstrate that continued
training and quality control measures are important for maintaining a high level of accuracy and
compliance with Federal requirements.

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. NHA-177 – APPROVING THE UNITED STATES
  DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT VETERANS
  AFFAIRS SUPPORTIVE HOUSING VOUCHER PROGRAM GRANT AWARD,
  RECEIVING FUNDING, AND AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2026/27
  OPERATING BUDGET BY INCREASING REVENUE ESTIMATES AND
  EXPENDITURES

Background:

The HUD-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH) program is a joint federal initiative
that provides Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) rental assistance to homeless Veterans and their
families, paired with case management and supportive services from the Department of
Veterans Affairs (VA). These services help participants secure and maintain permanent housing
while accessing essential healthcare and other supports to improve their quality of life.

VA provides case management and clinical services for participating Veterans at VA Medical
Centers (VAMCs), community-based outreach clinics (CBOCs), through VA contractors, or other
designated entities.

Congress has appropriated additional funding for new HUD-VASH vouchers every year since
2008.

Each year, HUD and VA jointly award HUD-VASH vouchers based on current geographic need
and public housing agency (PHA) performance. Since 2017, the allocation process for awarding
HUD-VASH vouchers has changed to allow PHAs to self-identify their interest in the program.
HUD publishes an annual HUD-VASH Registration of Interest Notice containing detailed
instructions that PHAs must follow if they are interested in receiving a portion of the available
 Norwalk Housing Authority  August 18, 2026
Resolution No. NHA-177 – HUD VASH Voucher  Page No. 2
Program

HUD-VASH vouchers. PHAs must have the support of a partnering VA facility and meet any
utilization threshold requirements to be eligible for an award. After the registration period closes,
HUD and VA use a formula to determine relative need and ultimately invite eligible PHAs to
apply for a specific number of HUD-VASH vouchers. The associated funding awarded for HUD-
VASH vouchers is determined by the actual average per-unit cost (PUC) at each PHA.

There is at least one PHA currently administering HUD-VASH in each of the 50 states, in the
District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, and Guam.

HUD-VASH vouchers are renewed based on actual PHA leasing, along with all other housing
choice vouchers (HCV). Details of annual renewal funding and potential set-aside fund
opportunities can be found in the annual HCV Funding Notice.

The HUD-VASH program is administered in accordance with regular HCV and PBV program
requirements (24 CFR Section 982 an 983, respectively).

Timeline:
On August 21, 2025, the Norwalk Housing Authority submitted a Registration of Interest for HUD-
VASH vouchers, as announced in Notice PIH 2025-21 (HA). The application process included
submitting a signed Letter of Support from the partnering VA Medical Center. After review, the
agency was awarded 18 VASH vouchers on March 21, 2026, with funding confirmed on June 25,
2026.

Therefore, staff is recommending that the Housing Commission accept the allocation of 18 HUD-
VASH vouchers and amend the budget to include a $313,356 Point of Obligation Benefit to
support the program's implementation and ongoing administration, enabling eligible veterans
and their families to access affordable housing and supportive services.

There is no fiscal impact on the General Fund. The NHA is funded solely by the United States
Department of Housing and Urban Development.

Program Requirements

  Your agency must follow all applicable Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program requirements
when administering HUD-VASH, including the regulations at 24 CFR parts 982 and 983, the
requirements in Notice PIH 2025-21 , and the guidance set forth in Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers:
Revised Implementation of the HUD-VASH Program published in the Federal Register
on August 13, 2024.
Financial Management Requirements
  The Financial Management Center (FMC) will provide your agency with an amended Annual
Contributions Contract that reflects the obligation of disbursement of funds. If your agency has any
questions regarding this funding obligation or disbursements, please contact your assigned FMC
Financial Analyst.

 Reporting Requirements
